title: Moby Dick Chapter 2 Action Spine Storyboard
adaptation_principle: One first-person action-spine sentence per frame. The image may be stylized and simplified, but it must not add unsupported narrative content. Named concepts in narration should be carried by caption and by character action, not by invented visual entities.
action_oriented_synopsis: Ishmael packs his carpet-bag and reaches New Bedford after the Nantucket packet has already gone. Because he still wants a Nantucket whaler, he must pass two cold nights and a day in New Bedford on very little money. He rejects the warmer, brighter inns as too expensive and follows the darker streets toward the waterfront. He mistakenly enters a church, realizes it is no lodging house, and backs out. He finds the poor, creaking Spouter-Inn, accepts the omen of Peter Coffin's name, and goes in.

frames.caption: With my old carpet-bag under my arm, I came to New Bedford on a black December Saturday, too late for the Nantucket packet.
frames.image_prompt: Ishmael steps into a wintry New Bedford waterfront street with an old carpet-bag tucked under his arm. The harbor is dark, the packet dock looks empty, and the night feels closed for travel. Show cold December darkness, shuttered waterfront buildings, and distant masts; do not show a whale, sea creature, or invented symbol. Leave clean negative space in the upper-left for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: Establish arrival, missed departure, and the practical problem that traps him in New Bedford.

frames.caption: My mind was made up for a Nantucket craft, so I had a night, a day, and another night to eat and sleep as cheaply as I could.
frames.image_prompt: Ishmael stands alone in the middle of a dreary New Bedford street, carpet-bag on his shoulder, gloved hand checking the few coins in his pocket. The north and south streets fall away into gloom. Keep the scene practical and human: cold, uncertainty, little money, no visible maps or explanatory labels. Leave clean negative space at the top-center for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: Turn the Nantucket preference into the concrete need for cheap food and lodging.

frames.caption: With only a few pieces of silver in my pocket, I passed the bright, jolly inns and kept waterward.
frames.image_prompt: Ishmael passes a warm, bright inn window spilling red-gold light onto hard packed snow while he keeps walking toward darker waterfront streets. His patched boots and thin coat show why he does not enter. The inn may have a hanging sign shape but no readable lettering. Do not add whale imagery or symbolic objects. Leave clean negative space in the bottom-right for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: Show his poverty choosing the route toward cheaper waterfront lodging.

frames.caption: In the dark streets I stumbled into a smoky church, found no bed there, and backed out again.
frames.image_prompt: Ishmael half-enters a low public doorway and stumbles over an ash-box in the porch; beyond the inner doorway, a dim candlelit church interior and a preacher at a pulpit make clear he has mistaken the place for lodging. Ishmael recoils and backs away. Keep faces generalized and respectful; the point is his mistake, not spectacle. Leave clean negative space in the upper-left for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: Compress the false start at "The Trap" into one clear action beat.

frames.caption: At last I found the creaking Spouter-Inn, with Peter Coffin's name beneath the sign, and took it for the cheap spot I needed.
frames.image_prompt: A shabby gable-ended wooden inn leans on a bleak corner near the docks, its hanging sign creaking in the wind with a crude painted spout of misty spray but no readable words. Ishmael stands below it with his carpet-bag, weighing the ominous, cheap-looking place. Do not show a whale, whale silhouette, sea creature, hunt, or invented emblem. Leave clean negative space in the upper-right for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: Establish the Spouter-Inn as the chosen lodging and carry the Coffin omen through caption rather than lettering.

frames.caption: No more blubbering; I scraped the ice from my frosted feet and went in to see what sort of place this Spouter might be.
frames.image_prompt: Close on Ishmael at the inn threshold, scraping ice from his boots before pushing open the rough door. Cold wind bends around the corner; warm dim light leaks from inside. Keep the action literal: feet, door, carpet-bag, winter street, no extra creatures or symbolic visions. Leave clean negative space in the bottom-center for the caption. No readable text.
frames.purpose: End the chapter on the physical decision to enter, handing off to chapter 3.
